title: Robot loop instrumentation
concept: A mobile robot repeatedly senses, estimates, plans, controls, and records state.
lab: Run the simulator for one minute and identify which dashboard metric changes first when the robot turns.
proof: Add one screenshot or one paragraph describing the robot loop.

title: Coordinate frames
concept: Robot pose is easier to debug when x, y, and heading are explicit.
lab: Change the starting pose and predict which direction the controller will command first.
proof: Record the starting pose and whether the prediction matched the trace.

title: PID tuning
concept: Proportional gain reduces heading error quickly, but too much can cause oscillation.
lab: Try low, medium, and high P gains. Compare overshoot and settling behavior.
proof: Record the gain values that produce the cleanest path trace.

title: Range-sensor noise
lab: Increase range noise and describe how it changes the closest-range metric.

title: A* route planning
concept: A* chooses cells by combining cost-so-far with estimated distance-to-go.
lab: Adjust planner clearance and watch the blocked-cell count and route length change.
proof: Record the clearance value, blocked-cell count, expanded-cell count, and route length.

title: Trace analysis
concept: A trace turns vague robot behavior into evidence.
lab: Use the route and trace to explain one failure or inefficiency.
proof: Write one bug-style note with expected behavior, actual behavior, and a hypothesis.

title: ROS2-style interface map
concept: Robotics systems are often organized as nodes that publish and subscribe to topics.
lab: Map the planner, sensor, controller, and telemetry modules to nodes and topics.
proof: Create a small node-topic-message table in the engineering log.

title: Planner tests
concept: Planning code needs edge-case tests because route failures are easy to miss visually.
lab: Read `src/robotics.test.ts` and add one new planner edge-case test.
proof: Commit the test and note what route bug it would catch.

title: Obstacle stress test
concept: The planner should fail clearly when no collision-free path exists.
lab: Add a blocking obstacle arrangement and confirm the planner reports fallback behavior.

title: Demo narrative
concept: A strong robotics project connects code choices to autonomy behavior.
lab: Update the README with one measurable planning or control result.
proof: Record route length, expanded cells, and the relevant test command.
